sentences.en: It is but seldom in actual life that the tragic and dramatic notes of action and feeling are struck with the force and frequency with which they were sounded in the Tichborne case.
sentences.zh: 在现实生活中，悲剧与戏剧性的行为和情感以如此震撼的力量和频率爆发，这种情况其实非常罕见，但在蒂奇伯恩案中却频频上演。

sentences.en: This strange episode, indeed, may be regarded as having been a species of moral tornado,
sentences.zh: 事实上，这段离奇的插曲可以被视为一场精神龙卷风，

sentences.en: which sweeping suddenly into the social midst swept men from their feet in its rushing and conflicting currents where excited every sort of human passion.
sentences.zh: 它突然席卷社交界，以汹涌交织的激流将人们冲得脚底不稳，并激发了各种各样的人类激情。

sentences.en: Prejudice.

sentences.en: Anger.

sentences.zh: 痛苦。

sentences.en: Sordid cupidity.
sentences.zh: 卑劣的贪婪。

sentences.en: Ambition.
sentences.zh: 野心。

sentences.en: Devotion.
sentences.zh: 奉献。

sentences.en: Cowardice.
sentences.zh: 怯懦。

sentences.en: Courage.
sentences.zh: 勇气。

sentences.en: In a word, every man's strength or weakness, the whole gamut of human motive and emotion raging and swirling about one large, melancholy, monstrous, mysterious figure.
sentences.zh: 总之，每个人的力量或弱点、人类动机与情感的整个音域都在一个庞大、忧郁、怪异、神秘的人物周围狂怒和盘旋。

sentences.en: So, Tom, those were the words of Arabella Keneally, who was a eugenicist,
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，那是阿拉贝拉·肯尼利的话，她是一位优生学家、

sentences.en: a novelist and anti-feminiSt. She was also the daughter of an eccentric Irish barrister called Edward Keneally.
sentences.zh: 小说家兼反女权主义者。她也是一位名叫爱德华·肯尼利的古怪爱尔兰大律师的女儿。

sentences.en: And she is talking about the Tichborne case, the greatest trial of Victorian England, arguably the most exciting and dramatic trial in all British history,
sentences.zh: 她谈论的是蒂奇伯恩案，这是维多利亚时代英格兰最伟大的审判，可以说是英国历史上最激动人心、最具戏剧性的审判，

sentences.en: which forms the centrepiece, as do those words, of Zadie Smith's brilliant novel, The Fraud, which you've been reading.
sentences.zh: 正如这些话一样，它是扎迪·史密斯你一直在读的精彩小说《欺诈》的核心。

sentences.en: Now, you don't normally read fiction, Tom, it's fair to say, because you don't like books that are imaginative.
sentences.zh: 话说回来，汤姆，你通常不读小说，这很公平，因为你不喜欢富有想象力的书。

sentences.en: Is that the case?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.zh: 我确实会为我们当代最伟大的小说家破例，多米尼克。

sentences.zh: 这是你对我说的话？

sentences.zh: 我的确在一次派对上碰巧遇到了扎迪。

sentences.en: Of course.

sentences.en: And she did mention that she had been writing a book on the Tichborne claimant.
sentences.zh: 她确实提到她一直在写一本关于蒂奇伯恩申诉人的书。

sentences.en: And my ears immediately pricked up.
sentences.zh: 我的耳朵立刻竖起来了。

sentences.en: Because as you say, this is an absolutely incredible story.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，这是一个绝对不可思议的故事。

sentences.en: I mean, it has curses, it has disputed inheritances, it has mad attempts to pass off various identities.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它有诅咒，有遗产纠纷，有冒充各种身份的疯狂企图。

sentences.en: And it's a case that obsesses Victorian Britain for years and years and years.
sentences.zh: 这是一个让维多利亚时代的英国着迷了整整好几年的案件。

sentences.en: So the moment The Fraud came out, I did indeed rush out and read it.

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她是现代英国获奖最多的小说家。

sentences.en: But what I will say is that it weaves in the facts of this extraordinary case with all kinds of meditations on fiction, on race, on empire, on all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 但我要说的是，它将这个非同寻常案件的事实与对小说、种族、帝国以及各种事物的各种思考交织在一起。

sentences.en: But it brilliantly articulates why this case obsessed people.
sentences.zh: 但它精彩地阐明了为什么这个案件会让人着迷。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是一位非常高产的维多利亚时代小说家，现在已经没人读他的书了。

sentences.en: Anyway, so this is a servant girl in his household who ends up marrying him.
sentences.zh: 总之，这是他家的一个女仆，最终嫁给了他。

sentences.en: And she becomes obsessed by the story of the Tichborn claimant.
sentences.zh: 她迷上了蒂奇伯恩申诉人的故事。

sentences.en: So no story captured her quite like the saga of the Tichborn claimant.
sentences.zh: 所以没有任何故事像蒂奇伯恩申诉人的传奇那样吸引她。

sentences.en: It had everything, toffs, Catholics, money, sex, mistaken identity and inheritance, high court judges, snobbery, exotic locations, the struggle of the honest working man,
sentences.zh: 里面应有尽有，权贵、天主教徒、金钱、性、身份错认与遗产、高等法院法官、势利、异国风情、诚实劳动者的奋斗，

sentences.en: as opposed to the undeserving poor and the power of a mother's love.
sentences.zh: 与不劳而获的穷人形成对比，还有母爱的力量。

sentences.en: So dramatic stuff, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 真是充满戏剧性，多米尼克。

sentences.en: And we thought, I mean, an ideal subject for the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 我们想过，我的意思是，这是“历史其余部分”的理想主题。

sentences.zh: 还有谁比扎迪·史密斯本人更适合谈论它呢？

sentences.zh: 通常当你上播客时，我想象人们会介绍你，然后马上把你请出来。

sentences.zh: 那么蒂奇伯恩案。

sentences.zh: 对于那些对此一无所知的人，我猜绝大多数人都是这样，首先用非常非常宽泛的术语，

sentences.zh: 解释一下它是什么，以及是什么吸引了你。

sentences.zh: 根据我的经验，我做过一些宣读。

sentences.zh: 当你开始试图解释这个案件时，事件本身就已经结束了。

sentences.zh: 但我会尽量快地讲完。

sentences.en: So a Catholic aristocrat young man called Sir Roger Tichborn.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫罗杰·蒂奇伯恩爵士的天主教贵族青年。

sentences.en: He was going to Jamaica.
sentences.zh: 他要去牙买加。

sentences.en: He was going on his kind of year off adventure.
sentences.zh: 他要去进行他那种间隔年式的冒险。

sentences.en: The boat went down with everybody on board.
sentences.zh: 船沉了，船上所有人都在内。

sentences.en: Everybody died.
sentences.zh: 所有人都死了。

sentences.en: But his mother, who was French and hated the family she'd married into, decided that he was still alive and put adverts all around England.
sentences.zh: 但他的母亲是法国人，讨厌她嫁入的家族，她坚信他还活着，并在全英国贴满广告，

sentences.en: And then all around Europe and finally all around Australia, offering larger and larger amounts of money for the return of her son, which seems unwise.
sentences.zh: 然后贴遍全欧洲，最后贴遍全澳大利亚，出价越来越高，只为找回她的儿子，这似乎很不理智。

sentences.en: And like a temptation to fraudsters.
sentences.zh: 就像是对骗子的诱惑。

sentences.en: And about 20 years later, a man does turn up with a black Jamaican with him, who was a servant of the Tichborn family.
sentences.zh: 大约20年后，确实有一个男人出现了，身边带着一个蒂奇伯恩家族的黑人仆人。

sentences.en: And together they arrive in Paris, where Roger's mother was, and say, well, I'm your son.
sentences.zh: 他们一起到达巴黎，也就是罗杰母亲所在的地方，并说，嗯，我是你的儿子。

sentences.en: And the problem with it was, was that the son was tall and thin.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，那个儿子又高又瘦。

sentences.en: This man, who was called Arthur Autumn, was about 300 pounds.
sentences.zh: 这个名叫亚瑟·奥顿的男人大约有300磅重。

sentences.en: He's a large man.
sentences.zh: 他是个大块头。

sentences.en: Very large man.
sentences.zh: 非常大的大块头。

sentences.en: The son was educated, grew up speaking French.
sentences.zh: 那个儿子受过教育，从小讲法语长大。

sentences.en: Arthur Autumn did not speak French, was not educated, was a butcher from Wapping, had a thick Cockney accent.
sentences.zh: 亚瑟·奥顿不会说法语，没受过教育，是瓦平的屠夫，有着浓重的伦敦腔。

sentences.en: Despite all of this, the mother said, that's my son.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，母亲还是说，那我的儿子。

sentences.en: For reasons maybe of perversity or of genuine longing.
sentences.zh: 原因可能是出于叛逆，也可能是出于真正的渴望。

sentences.en: Anyway, she said it, gave him a thousand pounds a year and then promptly died.
sentences.zh: 总之，她这么说了，给了他每年一千英镑，然后立马就去世了。

sentences.en: And that was the problem, starting an enormous court case because Sir Roger Tichborn was owed this enormous estate in Hampshire, but also like a substantial part of central London.
sentences.zh: 问题就在这里，引发了一场巨大的诉讼，因为罗杰·蒂奇伯恩爵士在汉普顿郡拥有一大笔遗产，而且还拥有伦敦市中心相当大的一部分。

sentences.en: All that bit around Tottenham Court Road, Doughty Street.
sentences.zh: 托特纳姆法院路、多蒂街周围的所有地方。

sentences.en: It was big.
sentences.zh: 太大了。

sentences.en: They'd married into the Doughty family, hadn't they?
sentences.zh: 他们和多蒂家族联姻了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Which had brought the Tichborns all this extra money and land.
sentences.zh: 这给蒂奇伯恩家族带来了所有这些额外的金钱和土地。

sentences.en: It was a double clan, a lot of land, a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 这是一个庞大的宗族，拥有大量的土地和金钱。

sentences.en: And so it started a court case that lasted for a year and a bit, at which point he was found to be lying.
sentences.zh: 于是开始了一场持续了一年多的诉讼，当时他被发现是在撒谎。

sentences.en: So then there was a criminal case after that.
sentences.zh: 之后又进行了一场刑事诉讼。

sentences.en: So altogether, it's about two and a half years in court.
sentences.zh: 总共在法庭上大约持续了两年半。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 所以这是在19世纪60年代和70年代，对吧？

sentences.zh: 它被报道在公报和各种八卦小报上。

sentences.en: The amazing thing about it is it captures the public imagination as much as it does, because from the way you described it,
sentences.zh: 神奇的是它如此引人入胜，因为从你的描述来看，

sentences.zh: 这听起来像是某种离奇的维多利亚时代案件，会在法庭上审理，最终谁会在乎呢。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 但实际上，正如汤姆刚才读的那段所暗示的。

sentences.zh: 它之所以有所有这些问题，是因为它涉及伦敦、澳大利亚。

sentences.zh: 他在南美遭遇海难了，对吧？

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.zh: 安德鲁·博格尔？

sentences.en: And giving testimony every day in court.
sentences.zh: 而且每天都在法庭上作证。

sentences.en: I mean, that was quite a sight.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那真是一场奇观。

sentences.en: I thought after I finished it, it kind of dawned on me that when you have a Jamaican, an Irish lawyer from Cork, who's very eccentric and a working class Englishman,
sentences.zh: 我写完后突然意识到，当你有一个牙买加人、一个来自科克郡且非常古怪的爱尔兰律师和一个工人阶级的英国人时，

sentences.en: you're basically dramatizing in the center of English power the whole problem of the 19th century, which is, oh, God, the Jamaicans.
sentences.zh: 你基本上是在英国权力的中心将19世纪的整个问题戏剧化，那就是，天哪，牙买加人。

sentences.en: Oh, God, the Irish.
sentences.zh: 天哪，爱尔兰人。

sentences.en: And oh, God, the working classes.
sentences.zh: 还有天哪，工人阶级。

sentences.en: These are three things that people aren't really wanting to think about.
sentences.zh: 这三件事是人们真正不想去想的。

sentences.en: And suddenly they're being dramatized daily in the Queen's Court.
sentences.zh: 而突然之间，它们每天都在女王的法庭上被戏剧化地上演。

sentences.en: It didn't really occur to me when I was writing it.
sentences.zh: 我在写的时候并没有真正想到这一点。

sentences.en: But when you step back, you can see the obsession.
sentences.zh: 但当你退后一步，你就能看出这种执念。

sentences.en: But also that sense of people from different classes and different backgrounds being brought together is very reminiscent of Dickens, who appears as a figure in your novel.
sentences.zh: 但那种来自不同阶层和背景的人聚在一起的感觉，也很容易让人想起狄更斯，他作为你小说中的一个人物出现。

sentences.zh: 那些是那种伟大的维多利亚时代大杂烩小说吗？

sentences.zh: 整个案件都有这种特质。

sentences.zh: 维多利亚小说里的任何法庭案件如果没有祖传诅咒都是不值得一提的。

sentences.zh: 更好的是，蒂奇伯恩申诉人案件带有一个据称可以追溯到12世纪的祖传诅咒。

sentences.zh: 我们能回到蒂奇伯恩救济粮的故事以及降临在蒂奇伯恩家族身上的诅咒吗？

sentences.en: I find this part of the story really disturbing because I like to think of myself as a rational actor interested in rational things.

sentences.en: But this story, it is a curse and it does come true.
sentences.zh: 但这个故事，它是一个诅咒，而且它真的应验了。

sentences.zh: 所以在几百年前，有一个前罗杰·蒂奇伯恩爵士，他有一个生病的妻子，玛贝拉夫人。

sentences.zh: 在她快死的时候，她对汉普郡的穷人感到担忧。

sentences.en: And she says she wants something to be kept for them.
sentences.zh: 她说她想为他们保留一些东西。

sentences.zh: 于是她决定，我真的不明白这其中的逻辑，但她决定在土地上爬行。

sentences.zh: 爬行？

sentences.zh: 嗯，她病得很重，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，我在特朗普出现之前就开始研究了，但这些类比是无法避免的。

sentences.en: And I think it's just because they're both studies in populism.
sentences.zh: 我想这只是因为它们都是民粹主义的研究样本。

sentences.en: And I think I got very used to the critique of right-wing populism, but this is something different.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我已经很习惯对右翼民粹主义的批判，但这是完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: This really is left-wing populism.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是左翼民粹主义。

sentences.en: It's quite irrational.
sentences.zh: 它是相当非理性的。

sentences.en: It's class-based.
sentences.zh: 它是基于阶级的。

sentences.en: But also, fascinatingly to me, it did work.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说同样迷人的是，它确实起作用了。

sentences.en: So one of the complaints of the people was that these courts were prejudiced against them, particularly the juries.
sentences.zh: 所以人们的不满之一是这些法庭对他们有偏见，尤其是陪审团。

sentences.en: And in the second trial, under this enormous public pressure and rhetoric, which was passing
sentences.zh: 而在第二次审判中，在关于法庭阶级制度的巨大公众压力和言论

sentences.en: around about the class-based system in the courts, the jury was then deliberately filled with only working people.
sentences.zh: 的推波助澜下，陪审团随后被刻意全部换成了劳动阶层的人。

sentences.en: And I think that might be one of the first times that happened in England.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能是英国历史上第一次发生这种事。

sentences.en: So it's an interesting case of what seems to be a deeply irrational, almost crazy case, working its way through a court and transforming it in some small way.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个有趣的案例，一个看起来极其不理性、近乎疯狂的案件，如何在法庭上运作并以某种微小的方式改变了法庭。

sentences.en: So I don't know, maybe it's an example of how populism, as frightening as it sometimes can be, does also function in some way and is a weird machine for manipulating people's
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道，也许这就是民粹主义的一个例子：尽管它有时会令人感到可怕，但它确实在某种程度上发挥了作用，并且是操纵人们

sentences.en: emotions to some political end.
sentences.zh: 情绪以达到某种政治目的的诡异机器。

sentences.en: And to what extent do you think this kind of vast populist enthusiasm for the claimant is making fantastical figures out of both the claimant and Andrew Bogle, who is the chief
sentences.zh: 你认为这种对原告铺天盖地的民粹主义狂热，在多大程度上把原告以及首席

sentences.en: substantiating witness?
sentences.zh: 证实证人安德鲁·博格尔塑造成了奇幻般的人物？

sentences.en: Because you give a kind of brilliant backstory of Andrew Bogle, of his father, who is taken from Africa and experience of the plantations before the abolition of slavery.
sentences.zh: 因为你对安德鲁·博格尔的身世做了精彩的背景介绍，他的父亲在废除奴隶制之前被从非洲带走并有过种植园的经历。

sentences.en: How much of that is based on fact?
sentences.zh: 其中有多少是基于事实的？

sentences.en: I mean, that's all fact.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那全都是事实。

sentences.en: I mean, everything that happens in the plantation scenes happens on those plantations.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，种植园场景中发生的一切都确确实实发生在那些种植园里。

sentences.en: And one of the amazing things about writing this book is that UCL have digitized every plantation in Jamaica, so you can get very granular, every name, every job, every child.
sentences.zh: 写这本书最神奇的事情之一就是伦敦大学学院将牙买加的每一个种植园都数字化了，所以你可以获得非常细致的信息，每一个名字、每一项工作、每一个孩子。

sentences.en: So we know exactly which plantation he was born on.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确切知道他出生在哪个种植园。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，对，完全如此。

sentences.en: He was on Hope and we have all the details.
sentences.zh: 他曾在希望种植园，我们拥有所有的细节。

sentences.en: So I had all the facts, which was an incredible thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我掌握了所有的事实，这真是一件不可思议的事。

sentences.en: But I think what interested me and interested Borges is like these Victorian lives that passed through so many situations.
sentences.zh: 但我认为吸引我和博格尔的是这些经历过如此多境遇的维多利亚时代的人生。

sentences.en: Like how extraordinary to be born in that situation and then come to London and find yourself in
sentences.zh: 出生在那样的环境中，然后来到伦敦发现自己身处高等法院，这是何等非凡的经历，

sentences.en: the high court, it was so hard to imagine what kind of a life was that, where you were in so many different worlds simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 很难想象那是怎样的一种生活，你同时身处如此之多的不同世界中。

sentences.en: But he did become a legend.
sentences.zh: 但他确实成了一个传奇。

sentences.en: And those meetings that Titchbourne or Arthur held all around the country, they were held
sentences.zh: 而蒂奇博恩或亚瑟在全国各地召开的那些集会，召开的地点

sentences.en: in the same places where, you know, for example, Dickens spoke, where political rallies were held.
sentences.zh: 和狄更斯演讲、举办政治集会的地方都是一样的。

sentences.en: They look like Trump rallies.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来就像特朗普的集会。

sentences.en: Like you turn up in town, hundreds and hundreds of people come.
sentences.zh: 就像你来到某个小镇，成百上千的人涌来。

sentences.en: There are banners, there are people screaming and shouting, and there's a lot of paraphernalia.
sentences.zh: 有横幅，有尖叫呐喊的人群，还有大量的周边道具。

sentences.en: Like if you go to junk stores now, you can still find little models of Bogle and Titchbourne, plates, cups.
sentences.zh: 就像你现在去旧货店，还能找到博格尔和蒂奇伯恩的小模型、盘子、杯子。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's extraordinary to me that it was that popular and then so completely forgotten.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得不可思议的是，它当时那么受欢迎，后来却被忘得这么干净。

sentences.en: That's the other thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是另一回事了。

sentences.en: And also they are fabricating witnesses, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 而且他们还在伪造证人，对吧？

sentences.en: So they come up with a Dane called Jean-Louis, who claims to have been a steward on the ship that had rescued Sir Roger from drowning and then taken him to Melbourne.
sentences.zh: 所以他们找来一个叫让-路易的丹麦人，他声称自己曾是那艘船上的服务员，那艘船救起了落水的罗杰爵士，然后把他带到了墨尔本。

sentences.en: He's a paid actor.
sentences.zh: 他是个花钱雇来的演员。

sentences.en: Yeah, a false flag, as they would say these days.
sentences.zh: 对，用现在的话说，就是虚假旗帜行动。

sentences.en: A recently released convict.
sentences.zh: 一个刚释放的罪犯。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're watching a court system in which it's perfectly normal to say we're going to have 210 witnesses.
sentences.zh: 对，你看到的审判系统里，说我们要传唤210名证人，这居然是完全正常的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So it wasn't a practical system.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是一个切实可行的系统。

sentences.en: And I think part of the effect of this trial was that the English legal system looked to itself and said, this can't continue.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这场审判的部分影响在于，英国法律体系审视自身后说，这不能再继续下去了。

sentences.en: You can't call 250 witnesses.
sentences.zh: 你不能传唤250名证人。

sentences.en: And this post-states, Jandice and Jandice, has Dickens already written Bleak House at this point?
sentences.zh: 而这已经是后《荒凉山庄》时代了，狄更斯这个时候已经写过《荒凉山庄》了吗？

sentences.en: One of the questions was, did Dickens go to this trial?
sentences.zh: 其中一个问题是，狄更斯去看过这场审判吗？

sentences.en: But then, of course, I realised he's dead just before it.
sentences.zh: 但后来，我当然意识到他在审判前不久就去世了。

sentences.en: He missed the trial that he would have adored.
sentences.zh: 他错过了这场他一定会迷恋至极的审判。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So Bleak House is 20 years before this, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以《荒凉山庄》实际上比这个早了20年。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: No, it's a perfectly Dickensian trial, but he is dead before it.
sentences.zh: 不，这是一场极其狄更斯式的审判，但他在这之前就去世了。

sentences.en: But Elliot is there.
sentences.zh: 但埃利奥特在。

sentences.en: George Elliot went to see it.
sentences.zh: 乔治·埃利奥特去看过。

sentences.en: I don't know what she made of it, but I love the idea of her sitting there watching this.
sentences.zh: 我不知道她对此作何感想，但我太喜欢她坐在那儿看着这一切的画面了。

sentences.en: It's much more Dickens than George Elliot, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这比乔治·埃利奥特的小说更像狄更斯，对吧？

sentences.en: The whole shenanigans.
sentences.zh: 整场闹剧。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's not to her taste at all.
sentences.zh: 对，这完全不合她的胃口。

sentences.en: She doesn't like this amount of irrationality and poor behaviour.
sentences.zh: 她不喜欢这种程度的荒谬和糟糕行为。

sentences.en: Very poor behaviour.
sentences.zh: 非常糟糕的行为。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We've had a lot of poor behaviour on the rest of this history, but we've never had poor behaviour like this.
sentences.zh: 我们在接下来的这段历史中见过很多糟糕行为，但我们从未见过像这样的糟糕行为。

sentences.en: So this is actually the longest trial in English history, I think, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是英国历史上历时最长的审判，我想是的吧？

sentences.en: I think MacLebel takes it, actually, in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 我觉得麦克莱布尔案超过了它，实际上是在90年代。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: But until...
sentences.zh: 但直到……

sentences.en: Until then, yeah.
sentences.zh: 直到那时，对。

sentences.en: It's the longeSt.
sentences.zh: 这是历时最长的。

sentences.en: But it actually ends so quickly.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上结束得那么快。

sentences.en: So there's a big issue of tattoos, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 所以这里有个关于纹身的大问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Of course there is.
sentences.zh: 当然有。

sentences.en: There's not the moment that basically this case falls apart because there's a bloke who was at boarding school with him.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个案子基本上土崩瓦解的时刻，因为有一个家伙曾和他一起上寄宿学校。

sentences.en: We always love a boarding school story, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我们总是喜欢寄宿学校的故事，汤姆。

sentences.en: Stonyhurst, is it?
sentences.zh: 斯托尼赫斯特，对吧？

sentences.en: Stonyhurst, a Jesuit boarding school.
sentences.zh: 斯托尼赫斯特，一所耶稣会寄宿学校。

sentences.en: I mean, who would go to a Jesuit boarding school?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，谁会去耶稣会寄宿学校？

sentences.en: Bonkers.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Anyway, that's by the by.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，那是题外话。

sentences.en: He's gone to this school and a bloke pitches up who says, I was at school with him and he had some very distinctive tattoos.
sentences.zh: 他去过这所学校，然后有个家伙跳出来说，我和他一起上过学，他有一些非常独特的纹身。

sentences.en: Seems odd that a teenager would have loads of tattoos, but well, who knows?
sentences.zh: 一个十几岁的少年身上有大量纹身，这似乎很奇怪，但好吧，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: And they did it to each other, maybe just inked each other.
sentences.zh: 而且他们可能是互相刺的，也许就是用墨水给对方纹的。

sentences.en: Inked each other?
sentences.zh: 互相纹身？

sentences.en: Yeah, inked each other.
sentences.zh: 对，互相纹身。

sentences.en: That sounds odd, but you know what I mean.
sentences.zh: 听起来很奇怪，但你知道我的意思。

sentences.en: Like probably your friends did it, but that's what did for him.
sentences.zh: 就像可能你的朋友也这么干过，但这正是害惨他的原因。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I think it's a bit like Trump and Stormy Daniels.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这有点像特朗普和斯托米·丹尼尔斯。

sentences.en: It's not the thing you think is going to take you down.
sentences.zh: 这不是你以为会把你拉下马的那种事。

sentences.en: It's always some...
sentences.zh: 总是一些……

sentences.en: Al Capone and the tax return.
sentences.zh: 阿尔·卡彭和纳税申报表。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's always some small thing.
sentences.zh: 对，总是一些小事。

sentences.en: And in the end, not having a tattoo on his arm...
sentences.zh: 而最后，他胳膊上没有纹身……

sentences.en: Was the killer.
sentences.zh: 才是致命一击。

sentences.en: Was the end of it, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是这一切的终结，对。

sentences.en: Because the jury say to the judge, we've heard enough.
sentences.zh: 因为陪审团对法官说，我们听够了。

sentences.en: We don't need the other 3,000 witnesses.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要那另外3000名证人了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's it.
sentences.zh: 对，就是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, two and a half years.
sentences.zh: 对，两年半。

sentences.en: We're good.
sentences.zh: 我们了解了。

sentences.en: It was a tattoo.
sentences.zh: 就是一个纹身。

sentences.en: And that was it.
sentences.zh: 然后就结束了。

sentences.en: And suddenly he was imprisoned for 14 years, I think.
sentences.zh: 突然之间他被判入狱14年，我想。

sentences.en: And by the time he was released, he was like a broken man.
sentences.zh: 到他出狱时，他就像个心碎欲绝、被彻底摧毁的人。

sentences.en: He then did confess to being Arthur Orton, to a newspaper to get some money.
sentences.zh: 他后来为了赚钱，向一家报社承认自己就是阿瑟·奥顿。

sentences.en: And with that money, set up a cigarette shop in Islington.
sentences.zh: 并用那笔钱在伊斯灵顿开了一家香烟店。

sentences.en: But years later, right?
sentences.zh: 但那是多年以后了，对吧？

sentences.en: Years later.
sentences.zh: 多年以后。

sentences.en: And paid by a newspaper.
sentences.zh: 而且是由报社花钱买的。

sentences.en: But then he retracts it, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 但后来他又翻供了，对吧？

sentences.en: And then he retracted it again.
sentences.zh: 然后他又一次翻供了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Still playing the game.
sentences.zh: 还在玩这套把戏。

sentences.en: And then died broke, destitute.
sentences.zh: 然后身无分文、一贫如洗地死去。

sentences.en: And then, to bring the story full circle, was buried right next to my house, which is how I came to know about all of this in the first place.
sentences.zh: 接着，为了让这个故事形成完整的闭环，他就埋在我家隔壁，这也是我一开始怎么知道这一切的原因。

sentences.en: In Paddington Cemetery off Wilsdon Lane.
sentences.zh: 在威尔斯登巷附近的帕丁顿公墓。

sentences.en: Is that so?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But buried as who?
sentences.zh: 但他是以谁的名义下葬的？

sentences.en: Well, this is the thing.
sentences.zh: 好了，关键就在这儿。

sentences.en: So when it was announced, he was going to be buried.
sentences.zh: 所以当时宣布他要下葬时。

sentences.en: And the case had been, you know, it was a long time since this had happened.
sentences.zh: 而且这个案子，你知道的，距离发生已经过去很久了。

sentences.en: And you'd think most people have forgotten about it.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得大多数人都已经把它忘了。

sentences.en: But suddenly, everybody was interested again.
sentences.zh: 但突然之间，所有人都重新关注起来。

sentences.en: And there's a photograph you can see online of 5,000 people in Wilsdon Lane.
sentences.zh: 你可以在网上看到一张照片，威尔斯登巷挤满了5000人。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: 5,000 came to see him buried.
sentences.zh: 5000人来看他下葬。

sentences.en: And the Tichborne family, for some reason, though they had fought him all those years, said, fair play.
sentences.zh: 而蒂奇伯恩家族不知出于什么原因，尽管他们跟他斗了那么多年，还是说，算了吧，公平竞争。

sentences.en: You can have a little cardboard thing on top of the coffin saying Sir Roger Tichborne.
sentences.zh: 你们可以在棺材上放一个写着“罗杰·蒂奇伯恩爵士”的小纸牌。

sentences.en: That's nice of them.
sentences.zh: 他们人还怪好的。

sentences.en: That's so bizarre, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这太离奇了，对吧？

sentences.en: It's so bizarre.
sentences.zh: 太离奇了。

sentences.en: And he was buried in a pauper's grave.
sentences.zh: 而且他是被埋在穷人墓地里的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There was no money to bury him.
sentences.zh: 没有钱给他办葬礼。

sentences.en: And there's no stone.
sentences.zh: 而且没有墓碑。

sentences.en: So it wasn't that official.
sentences.zh: 所以并没有那么正式。

sentences.en: But apparently, they let this little cardboard sign.
sentences.zh: 但显然，他们允许放这个小纸牌。

sentences.en: Why did they do that?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: That's mad.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: It's sentimental or Dominic or guilt.
sentences.zh: 是出于感伤、仁慈还是内疚？

sentences.en: Were they admitting, yeah, guilt.
sentences.zh: 难道他们是在承认，是的，有罪吗。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So there he lies.
sentences.zh: 他就那样躺在那里。

sentences.en: And I walk past him every day with the dog in this pauper's grave.
sentences.zh: 我每天带着狗从这个穷人墓地旁走过。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And what happens to Andrew Bogle?
sentences.zh: 那安德鲁·博格尔怎么样了？

sentences.en: Borges said he was run over in King's Cross, but that's a romance.
sentences.zh: 博格尔说他在国王十字车站被车撞了，但这只是一种浪漫的说法。

sentences.en: It's not true.
sentences.zh: 不是真的。

sentences.zh: 他只是在国王十字车站穷困潦倒地死去，同样埋在穷人墓地里。

sentences.en: His mixed race son had had, by that point, 11 children.
sentences.zh: 他的混血儿子到那时已经有了11个孩子。

sentences.en: So I always assume there are a lot of Bogle's in England.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是假设英国有很多姓博格尔的人。

sentences.en: They're probably white, or they might be any other color.
sentences.zh: 他们可能是白人，也可能是其他任何肤色。

sentences.en: I guess they might have married whoever, but they might not know that they are related to this extraordinary man.
sentences.zh: 我想他们可能跟任何人结过婚，但他们可能并不知道自己跟这个非凡的男人有亲戚关系。

sentences.en: And what about Titchborns?
sentences.zh: 那蒂奇伯恩家族呢？

sentences.en: The Titchborns continue, I think.
sentences.zh: 蒂奇伯恩家族延续了下来，我想是的。

sentences.en: There's a few Titchborn pubs in Hampshire, which I still haven't visited, which I'm excited by.
sentences.zh: 汉普郡还有几家叫蒂奇伯恩的酒吧，我还没去过，对此我很期待。

sentences.en: The house, I know, doesn't belong to them anymore because I saw it in the Sunday Times for sale one day.
sentences.zh: 我知道那栋房子已经不属于他们了，因为有一天我在《星期日泰晤士报》上看到它在出售。

sentences.en: Not for very much money, even.
sentences.zh: 甚至没卖多少钱。

sentences.en: Oh, go for it.
sentences.zh: 哦，买下它吧。

sentences.en: No, I don't think it has much land left.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得它没剩多少土地了。

sentences.en: I think it's just the house now.
sentences.zh: 我想现在只剩下那栋房子了。

sentences.en: There must be Titchborns around, but I don't think their wealth continued.
sentences.zh: 周围肯定还有蒂奇伯恩家族的人，但我认为他们的财富并没有延续下去。

sentences.en: And I don't know if they still get the rents from Doughty Street.
sentences.zh: 我也不知道他们是否还能从道蒂街收到租金。

sentences.en: The Baronetcy has expired.
sentences.zh: 准男爵爵位已经失效了。

sentences.en: I'm looking at it here.
sentences.zh: 我正看着呢。

sentences.en: Yes, that's it.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是这样。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 你看。

sentences.en: Sir Anthony Doughty, Titchborn.
sentences.zh: 安东尼·道蒂·蒂奇伯恩爵士。

sentences.en: And so one last legacy of this case is our word, Titchy.
sentences.zh: 所以这个案子留下的最后一个遗产就是我们的一个词，“小不点”（Titchy）。

sentences.en: Yeah, that part is crazy.
sentences.zh: 对，那部分太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And for the relief of my readers, I did not add another 58 pages on this topic.
sentences.zh: 为了让我松一口气，读者们，我没有在这个话题上再多写58页。

sentences.en: I restrained myself, which I thought was good.
sentences.zh: 我克制住了自己，我觉得这挺好。

sentences.en: But there was a music hall figure who apparently looked a bit like Arthur Orton in the face
sentences.zh: 但当时有个音乐厅艺人，外表长得显然有点像阿瑟·奥顿，

sentences.en: and was quite round, but with the key difference of being four foot six, which is really quite small.
sentences.zh: 体型也挺圆润，但关键的区别在于他身高只有四尺六寸（约137厘米），真的非常矮。

sentences.en: And he was called Little Titch and was a massive music hall star, performed in blackface a lot of the time, which is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 他叫小蒂奇（Little Titch），是音乐厅里的大明星，演出时经常涂黑脸，这很迷人。

sentences.en: But his most famous routine was with these two massive ski feet.
sentences.zh: 但他最著名的绝活是踩着两只巨大无比的滑雪板似的大鞋子。

sentences.en: He was called Big Boots.
sentences.zh: 他被称为大靴子。

sentences.en: And he would do a big boot dance in which, you know, that bit in Smooth Criminal where
sentences.zh: 他会跳一段大靴子舞，你知道的，就像《犯罪高手》（Smooth Criminal）里的那个片段，其中

sentences.en: Michael Jackson goes all the way to the floor almost and back again.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·杰克逊几乎能把身体压到贴地，然后再直起来。

sentences.en: Little Titch did that firSt.
sentences.zh: 小蒂奇最早就是这么干的。

sentences.en: On the skis, he would go all the way to the floor and back.
sentences.zh: 滑雪的时候，他也能整个人压到贴地再起来。

sentences.en: There's a video of it.
sentences.zh: 网上有这方面的视频。

sentences.en: You can see online.
sentences.zh: 你可以在网上看到。

sentences.en: And he was an incredible hit.
sentences.zh: 而且他当时大受欢迎、红极一时。

sentences.en: So we still say things are Titchy because of Little Titch.
sentences.zh: 所以直到现在，我们还因为小蒂奇而用“蒂奇”来形容个子矮小。

sentences.en: Yeah, I had a friend at school when I was eight.
sentences.zh: 对啊，我八岁上学时有个朋友。

sentences.en: I mean, he was just called Titch.
sentences.zh: 我是说，大家就叫他“蒂奇”。

sentences.en: Everyone called him Titch.
sentences.zh: 所有人都叫他蒂奇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And it never occurred to me.
sentences.zh: 而且我从来没想过。

sentences.en: Yeah, or where that word came from.
sentences.zh: 对啊，也没想过这个词是哪来的。

sentences.en: That he was called Little Titch after the Titchborn claimant.
sentences.zh: 他被称为“小蒂奇”是因为蒂奇伯恩冒名顶替案。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Kind of perfect that this very music hall trial ends up in the music hall.
sentences.zh: 这个关于音乐厅的审判最后又回到了音乐厅，真是挺奇妙的。

sentences.en: Yeah, still with all the same themes around it, the idea of, you know, this blackface character who's channeling some unseen place that nobody visits and nobody knows about.
sentences.zh: 是啊，周围探讨的主题依然没变，你知道的，就是这种黑脸滑稽演员的角色，他仿佛在传导某种无人涉足、无人知晓的神秘领域。

sentences.en: All the themes just keep on circling.
sentences.zh: 所有的主题一直在盘旋反复。

sentences.en: Center of England, the things on the border, and these strange, irrational actors.
sentences.zh: 英国的中心，边缘地带的事物，还有这些奇怪、荒谬的演员。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 对，太迷人了。

sentences.en: Just a question before we go, Zadie, about your book, The Fraud.
sentences.zh: 在结束之前，扎迪，有个关于你的书《骗局》的问题想问问你。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So obviously, you know, we've done however many episodes about history.
sentences.zh: 显然，你知道的，我们已经做了无数期关于历史的节目了。

sentences.en: We sometimes talk about historical fiction.
sentences.zh: 我们有时会谈到历史小说。

sentences.en: So we talk about Patrick O'Brien or whoever it might be.
sentences.zh: 我们会聊帕特里克·奥布莱恩或者其他什么作家。

sentences.en: But for you as a novelist, writing about a period of history, do you feel a kind of obligation to the, you know, this is such a detailed story.
sentences.zh: 但对你这位小说家来说，在书写一段历史时期时，你是否会觉得有一种责任感，因为你知道，这是一个细节极其丰富的的故事。

sentences.en: There are, as it were, so many facts.
sentences.zh: 可以说，里面有这么多的事实。

sentences.en: Do you feel an obligation, a responsibility to keep to the facts?
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得自己有义务、有责任坚守事实？

sentences.en: Or do you feel as a novelist, you have free reign, as it were?
sentences.zh: 还是说，作为一个小说家，你觉得可以自由驰骋？

sentences.en: I remember hearing Hilary talk about this, Mantel, and I think she's right.
sentences.zh: 我记得听希拉里·曼特尔谈过这个，我觉得她说的对。

sentences.en: If you want to work with history, you want to work with history.
sentences.zh: 如果你想以历史为素材，你就得去处理历史。

sentences.en: The facts are important.
sentences.zh: 事实很重要。

sentences.en: They're very important to me.
sentences.zh: 对我很重要。

sentences.en: So I wouldn't see the point of manipulating them beyond reason.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得没有必要无理取闹地去篡改它们。

sentences.en: And in this case, you barely had to fictionalize.
sentences.zh: 而且在这个故事里，你几乎不需要怎么虚构。

sentences.en: It is a fiction in itself.
sentences.zh: 它本身就是一个充满戏剧性的传奇。

sentences.en: And I didn't change anything, really.
sentences.zh: 我其实没怎么改动。

sentences.en: The only change is a fictional character outside of the case called Mrs. Touche, who is kind of extended beyond her normal lifespan or realm.
sentences.zh: 唯一的改动是一个案子之外虚构的角色，叫杜谢太太，她的寿命或活动范围被适度延伸了。

sentences.en: But no, to me, the facts are really important.
sentences.zh: 但说真的，对我而言，事实真的非常重要。

sentences.en: It's like a rearrangement of the facts into fiction, but not an obscuring or a changing of them.
sentences.zh: 这就像是对事实进行文学化的重新排列，而不是去掩盖或改变它们。

sentences.en: It's the truth that fascinates me.
sentences.zh: 真正吸引我的是真相。

sentences.en: But it's also a novel about Victorian novels to a degree, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但从某种程度上说，这也是一部关于维多利亚时代小说的书，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I think I was just kind of interested in everything that Victorian novels hide or obscure.
sentences.zh: 我想我只是对维多利亚时代小说所隐藏或掩盖的一切比较感兴趣。

sentences.en: Like it's so common in a Victorian novel for the most useless son of the family to disappear to Jamaica or to Australia.
sentences.zh: 比如在维多利亚时代的小说里，家里最没用的儿子跑去牙买加或者澳大利亚，这实在是太常见了。

sentences.en: And it's always out of sight.
sentences.zh: 而且总是消失在视线之外。

sentences.en: You never quite know where these useless sons are going to.
sentences.zh: 你永远搞不清这些没用的儿子究竟去了哪里。

sentences.en: So it was an opportunity for me to kind of know myself, to fill in those gaps and write it in full.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我来说是个机会，让我能去探索，去填补那些空白，把故事完整地写出来。

sentences.en: But the energy of those Victorian novels and the incredible kind of imaginative engine of them is something I've envied all my life.
sentences.zh: 但维多利亚时代小说里的那种活力，以及它们惊人的想象力引擎，是我一向艳羡的。

sentences.en: They're such incredible generators of story.
sentences.zh: 它们是如此了不起的故事制造机。

sentences.en: Well, you have done them proud.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你没让它们失望。

sentences.en: So Zadie Smith, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 那么，扎迪·史密斯，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I loved it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: The novel, the fraud is absolutely unmissable.
sentences.zh: 这部小说《骗局》绝对不容错过。

sentences.en: We hope you have enjoyed this extraordinary story.
sentences.zh: 我们希望你喜欢这个非同寻常的故事。

sentences.en: And who knows, the claimant, real or not, you decide.
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢，那个冒名顶替者是真是假，由你来决定。

sentences.en: Thanks very much for listening.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢收听。

sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 再见。
